facts.claim: In the Letzler–Tasoff experiment, expected rebate redemption exceeded actual redemption by 49 percentage points.
facts.mechanism: This mechanism operates because participants underweighted the future hassle of completing and returning the form.
facts.commonError: Low rebate redemption proves buyers never intended to claim the money.
facts.whyWrong: Their elicited expectations were much higher than their eventual completion.

facts.claim: The HAIL Scholarship promised four years of tuition and fees to targeted high-achieving, low-income Michigan students who were admitted.
facts.mechanism: This mechanism operates because an early unconditional-looking guarantee removed uncertainty about affordability before application effort was due.
facts.commonError: HAIL relaxed the university's academic admission standard.
facts.whyWrong: The intervention changed outreach and aid certainty, not eligibility for admission.

facts.claim: US federal paperwork requirements were estimated at roughly eleven billion public burden hours annually.
facts.mechanism: This mechanism operates because each form, record, and reporting rule consumes time across millions of affected people and organizations.
facts.commonError: A form is costless when the government charges no filing fee.
facts.whyWrong: Time and cognitive effort remain real resources.

facts.claim: An unsubscribe trap makes joining substantially easier than leaving the same service.
facts.mechanism: This mechanism operates because the firm places friction only on the action that reduces its revenue.
facts.commonError: A difficult cancellation process merely reflects equal administrative needs in both directions.
facts.whyWrong: The asymmetry reveals that equivalent account changes receive different burdens.

facts.claim: Mail-in rebate redemption rates commonly fall between 10 and 40 percent.
facts.mechanism: This mechanism operates because deadlines, forms, documentation, and forgetting prevent many purchasers from completing the later task.
facts.commonError: The advertised rebate reduces the effective price for nearly every buyer.
facts.whyWrong: Only completed claims receive the money.

facts.claim: A shrouded attribute is a costly product feature that remains difficult to discover when the headline price is shown.
facts.mechanism: This mechanism operates because sellers make the base product salient and defer attention to complementary costs such as printer ink.
facts.commonError: A low printer purchase price demonstrates a low total ownership cost.
facts.whyWrong: Replacement cartridges can dominate the lifetime expense.

facts.claim: Administrative burden can reduce benefit take-up among people who are legally eligible.
facts.mechanism: This mechanism operates because forms, documentation, waiting, and uncertainty impose costs before the benefit is received.
facts.commonError: Low take-up proves that eligible people do not value the program.
facts.whyWrong: Noncompletion can reflect process cost rather than preference.

facts.claim: A sludge audit inventories time, steps, confusion, and psychological costs before deciding what to remove.
facts.mechanism: This mechanism operates because making each burden explicit allows necessary safeguards to be separated from inherited or self-serving friction.
facts.commonError: A sludge audit begins by deleting every verification step.
facts.whyWrong: Some burdens protect safety, privacy, or program integrity and must be justified rather than automatically removed.

facts.claim: Prefilling tax returns with information government already possesses can reduce duplicate reporting.
facts.mechanism: This mechanism operates because reusing wage and withholding data removes transcription and search tasks from the taxpayer.
facts.commonError: Prefilling prevents taxpayers from correcting government errors.
facts.whyWrong: A prefilled return can remain reviewable and editable.
